D: A boy befriends a giant robot that eats metal.
P: Serve the mains when Hogarth hides the giant in Dean's junkyard.
S: Annie works the late shift at the diner while Hogarth hides a giant

Clams, potato and smoky bacon in a creamy broth, served in mugs with crackers. Fry 4 rashers diced bacon until crisp, add 1 diced onion and 2 diced celery sticks and soften. Stir in 2 tbsp plain flour, then 500ml fish stock, 400g diced potatoes and a bay leaf and simmer 15 minutes. Add 1kg vongole, cover and cook 5 minutes until they open, then pull most of the meat from the shells. Stir in 250ml cream, warm through, season and serve with crackers.
The government man from Washington, who moves into Hogarth's spare room

Hard-boiled eggs filled with a creamy mustard yolk, piped high and dusted with paprika and chives. Boil 8 eggs for 10 minutes, cool in iced water and peel. Halve and mash the yolks with 4 tbsp mayonnaise, 2 tsp Dijon mustard, 1 tsp white vinegar, salt and pepper. Pipe or spoon back into the whites, dust with smoked paprika and scatter with snipped chives.
M: Beef and pork meatloaf with tomato glaze, served with mash and peas
Beef and pork mince with breadcrumbs, egg and onion, tomato glaze, baked at 180C for an hour, mash and peas.
Rockwell, Maine, 1957, where the Giant comes down by the harbour

Lobster tossed in a little mayonnaise, lemon and chives, piled into buttered toasted rolls, with potato chips and a pickle. Chop the lobster and mix with the mayonnaise, celery, a squeeze of lemon and chopped chives. Butter the outside of the rolls and toast in a hot pan until golden. Pile the lobster into the rolls and serve with chips and a pickle.
W: Crunchy peanut brittle broken into jagged shards, brushed with edible silver

Golden peanut brittle smashed into jagged sheets like scrap from Dean's yard, with flaky salt and a silver dusting of edible lustre. Line a tray with baking paper. Heat 300g caster sugar, 120ml liquid glucose and 80ml water in a heavy pan to 150C on a sugar thermometer. Take off the heat and quickly stir in 250g roasted peanuts, 20g butter and 1 tsp bicarb soda. Pour onto the tray and spread thin. Sprinkle with flaky salt and brush lightly with silver edible lustre. Cool 30 minutes, then smash into jagged shards.
Muffin tin apple pies with cinnamon and a lattice top
Mini apple pies in a muffin tin, shortcrust cases filled with spiced apple, lattice tops, baked at 190C for 25 minutes.
Almond and orange biscotti baked twice until crisp
Dough of flour, sugar, eggs, almonds and orange zest shaped into a log, baked at 170C for 25 minutes, sliced, baked again 10 minutes a side until crisp.
K: Espresso, vanilla ice cream and malt blended thick, topped with whipped cream

Vanilla ice cream blended with a shot of espresso, milk and malt, poured thick and topped with whipped cream and chocolate-covered coffee beans. Brew 2 shots espresso and cool, or use decaf for younger kids. Blend with 8 scoops vanilla ice cream, 400ml cold milk and 3 tbsp malted milk powder for 30 seconds until thick. Pour into 4 tall glasses. Top each with whipped cream and a few chocolate-coated coffee beans, or chocolate sprinkles for the little ones.

Boil and mash the potatoes with butter and cook the peas.

steps.text: Cook the apples with the sugar and cinnamon until soft, then cool.
Cut rounds from two pastry sheets and line a 12-hole muffin tin. Fill with the apple.
Cut the third sheet into strips and lay a lattice over each.
Bake at 190C until golden.
Mix the flour, sugar, baking powder, eggs, almonds and orange zest into a dough.
Shape into a log on a lined tray.
Bake at 170C.
Cool, slice and bake again, turning once.
Cool completely to crisp up.
Brew the espresso and cool.
Blend with the ice cream, milk and malted milk powder until thick.
Pour into four tall glasses and top with whipped cream and chocolate-coated coffee beans, or sprinkles for little ones.
